M-045.Name: ExtensionHost
M-045.Summary: Extension host module: manifest parsing/validation, extension discovery (scan installed bundles), registry (enable/disable, state persistence), auth (keychain-based shared secret via M-019), invocation (HTTP POST to 127.0.0.1 per D1), and live document server (axum HTTP endpoint for stream.document). First consumer: TokMo meeting intelligence extension. C-15 T-103: live_endpoint is_pid_alive has a Windows tasklist arm (was assume-stale) and platform labels windows-x86_64/aarch64; discovery scans %APPDATA% on Windows. C-SEC-AUDIT-FIXES: the three existing incoming data routes require bearer authentication for an enabled extension; text-insert additionally requires text.insert and emits the authenticated requester identity. Candidate capabilities are snapshotted before credential lookup outside the registry lock and off the async executor. Successful disable first fences enabled state, then revokes and verifies absence in persistent and memory stores; failures remain visible and fresh pairing restores access. Both outgoing clients parse and revalidate loopback URLs with no userinfo, refuse redirects and bypass proxy environment settings. Pair bootstrap, stream sessions and listener surface remain unchanged. C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH and C-SEC-STREAM-TABS: stream routes require an enabled registered identity and validate its authorization generation and session owner/incarnation at a serialized mutation boundary. Disable closes only its active stream before credential revocation, including deletion failure. Foreign-owner open conflicts disclose no session ID; same-owner resync remains supported. Ordered open/patch/close events all carry session_id and a monotonic session_epoch, and the renderer routes them through owned store actions.

notes.note-2: Extension secrets stored via M-019 datacenter keychain. Never build a separate secret store.

notes.note-5: Live-doc wire contract v2 (breaking): /stream/open sends sections as an ordered array of {name, content} with real initial content; document_md is the authoritative join of sections (initial_md advisory). /stream/patch carries op: "append" | "replace" ("replace_section" accepted as synonym, missing op defaults to "replace"); section content is self-contained markdown — Mark never adds headers; unknown op or unknown section is rejected with 400. Document rebuild is deterministic: declared section order, empty sections skipped, "\n\n" separator. Recovery: /stream/open with the SAME session_id on an active session replaces state wholesale (resync path, log BLOCK_DOC_OPEN_RESYNC) — the escape hatch for a client stuck on needs_resync; a DIFFERENT session_id still gets 409. TokMo is the only consumer; both apps ship together.

M-046.Summary:
C-ATTRIBUTION-NOTICE-REFRESH: the Node notice formatter counts third-party rows after root exclusion and documents the exact installed checker command; Node and Rust notices are regenerated from complete pinned offline tool outputs, without a custom collector or dependency changes. C-RELEASE-PIPELINE-AUTOMATION (2026-10-20): M-046 now owns the repository release train authority, release preparation and atomic JSON/Markdown train-ledger plus version normalization, exact README/CHANGELOG/release-note/What's New material checks, payload-to-seal readiness, the public one-way Project mirror, owner-local GitHub control reconciliation, input-free owner-approved annotated-tag promotion, tag-only signing, read-only publication-bundle preparation, fixed-command digest-verified draft-first publication, and an idempotent downstream cask handoff. C-RELEASE-PIPELINE-CLOSEOUT records the public Project identity, activates the reviewed main/tag rulesets, and extends the cask handoff with tap-owned validation plus exact-bot-PR auto-merge behind the required check; Projects remains a non-authoritative one-way mirror. Tag admission restores the remote annotated tag object after checkout rewrites its local tag ref to the peeled commit, then proves the restored object targets the checked-out seal before packaging. Promotion preserves complete main ancestry before both strict admission passes so payload-to-seal merge-base evidence is available on hosted runners. C-RELEASE-CONVEYOR (2026-10-24): Release Please is retired — package.json, set by npm version in the reviewed preparation PR, is the single version authority and normalization propagates it; the current train is named once in docs/release-trains/current.json and resolved by tools/release-train.mjs; the payload-to-seal span may hold any number of bookkeeping-only commits (each proven, merges judged against their first parent); promotion binds to a seal that is on main rather than main's exact tip; publication itself proves the releases/latest feed advanced. Manual dispatch is unsigned build-only; Projects never becomes gate authority; secrets and admin apply are isolated by purpose. The pull-request Tauri dry-run also remains unprivileged: it disables updater artifacts through a narrow CLI config override while retaining .app/DMG packaging, ad-hoc signing, install smoke, size and warning evidence. Production tag builds keep updater artifacts enabled and receive the updater private key only inside release-signing. Retained synthetic preference JSON and its manifest use LF checkout bytes; privacy verification normalizes host path separators and accepts manifest line delimiters on Windows, macOS and Linux.
C-ACCEPTANCE-REGISTRY (2026-10-21): M-046 admission gains an ordered evidence trail — docs/acceptance/registry.json registers every isolated test artifact (source sha, bundle identity, binary digest, build recipe via tools/build-test-artifact.mjs) and every review wave and owner verdict per delivery item; tools/acceptance-registry.mjs --check enforces schema, git sha resolvability and two-way consistency with the collecting train inside the standard vitest matrix (V-M-046). vitest.int.config.mjs re-exports the canonical Vitest configuration for portable historical C-71 commands, without machine-specific paths. C-FIX-013: the canonical vitest config guards Node >= 25 default-on experimental Web Storage with a conditional test.execArgv (--no-experimental-webstorage, passed only on major >= 25 so the Node 22 reference runtime keeps byte-identical worker arguments) so the jsdom localStorage implementation stays authoritative; .nvmrc pins the Node 22 reference runtime. The test workflow gates session restore and close/edit ownership in WKWebView's browser engine through webkit-session. The test workflow also gates C-68 diff priority/opened-baseline regressions through the webkit-diff project. The test workflow gates native Shift+Up/Down selection with the passive format toolbar through the webkit-keyboard project. C-CI-CD-AUDIT-FIXES: the required renderer-unit result includes IPC type checking; the WebKit theme/tree projects run once each while screenshot upload remains. Manual QA runs each check as a separate fail-fast step and disables updater artifacts without release keys. The docs-only classifier checks out the tree, has PR read permission, and treats mixed code/documentation changes as full-test candidates. Local, CI, QA and release packaging use Rust 1.99.0 and immutable Actions revisions, with toolchain-sensitive Rust cache keys. C-63: the test workflow explicitly gates the C-60 footnote and C-62 diagram-appearance projects in WebKit after browser installation, preserving their WKWebView-engine coverage on every test run. M-064.Name: RepositorySafetyGate
M-064.Summary:
C-PUBLIC-REPOSITORY-HYGIENE keeps the public gate deterministic and portable. It snapshots exact staged trees, commit messages, outgoing commits and ref updates; rejects reserved/private paths, credentials, personal absolute paths, private infrastructure, unsupported binaries, unsafe lane crossings, AI attribution and AI-prefixed branch names; runs Gitleaks with trusted defaults; rebuilds the candidate identity after the scan; and stores a private hash-bound receipt in the common Git directory.
C-SAFE-SCREENSHOT-REVIEW admits only regular README PNG bytes whose exact SHA-256 identity and completed human visual review are present in a changed release screenshot manifest in the same commit. Outgoing commits are evaluated independently; every other binary stays blocked. Deletion-only branch housekeeping is admitted only for non-main tips proven merged into remote main. C-MESSAGE-ONLY-HISTORY-REWRITE-V3 adds a message-only main rewrite lane bound to an exact owner-local manifest. It proves paired ordered-parent DAGs and raw headers, preserves every tree and identity, and permits only approved message replacements plus the explicitly counted removal of GPG signatures invalidated by new commit identities. Its recovery phase admits a single desktop PR rebase only when the live old branch tip and live main read from the actual push endpoint match the negotiated and remote-tracking identities, the new head descends from that main, and every replayed commit unique to the rebuilt branch passes the normal push scan. The endpoint is never retained in review payloads, receipts or diagnostics.
C-SAFETY-GATE-MODEL-REVIEW restored the exact-candidate model review with owner-local configuration and the explicit human override; C-SAFETY-LOCAL-FIRST-REVIEW (owner policy of 2026-10-31) now runs it as one local-first pass per chunk. The gate resolves a single executor — the optional offload endpoint when a bounded health probe proves it ready (reachable, not redirecting, empty slot or the expected model), otherwise the owner-local reviewer — and a missing, powered-off, unreachable or busy offload host never blocks an operation. The offload endpoint must resolve to a private or overlay address; a public or redirecting endpoint is a configuration error before any inference; a malformed verdict, a different loaded model or an unreachable resolved executor fails closed. An explicit human MARK_SAFETY_OVERRIDE skips only the model phase and writes an identity-bound private receipt. The deterministic boundary also rejects owner-workspace and private-companion references.

Contract.Purpose: Stop a local commit or push unless the exact complete candidate passes deterministic exposure, lane, Gitleaks and identity checks plus one local-first single-pass model review with an optional offload executor, including manifest-bound screenshot evidence, exact-manifest proof for an approved message-only main rewrite, and push-endpoint live-tip/current-main proof for a rebuilt desktop PR branch.

Input.Name: candidate
Input.Type: staged tree/message, independently grouped outgoing commits, a push-endpoint/current-main-bound desktop PR rebase, or paired raw commit DAGs plus an owner-local rewrite manifest

Output.Name: decision
Output.Type: pass or fail with redacted markers and private hash-bound evidence

Error.Description: Exposure, private-companion reference, incomplete evidence, unsupported payload, changed candidate, missing, unreachable, public, redirecting, slot-ambiguous or non-passing model reviewer, stale or shallow history, missing push endpoint, stale branch/main identity, unbased desktop PR rebase, rewrite manifest/DAG/header/signature mismatch, an unproven branch deletion, AI attribution, or an AI-named branch.

M-068.Name: RollbackManager
M-068.Summary: One-step updater rollback (C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK): before every in-app update the running version is snapshotted (macOS: staged .app copy + preferences snapshot with SHA-256 digests in a strict manifest under the M-022 data root; Windows: version-only manifest, the restore fetches the previous installer by its deterministic release asset name and verifies the minisignature from that release's latest.json against the app-pinned updater pubkey — exactly two fetches). Verification strictly precedes any mutation on both platforms (C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES): every check — snapshot parse, staged-bundle digest, Windows fetch/version/minisignature — passes before the first write, so a failure aborts with the previous state untouched. The macOS bundle swap is reversible with no half-swap state: the running bundle is renamed aside as {stem}.rollback-aside, the staged bundle renamed into the running path, and only after that rename confirms is the departed bundle moved to Trash; a failure before the confirmed replacement rolls the aside back. Boot reconciliation is promote-only-after-confirmed-replacement: the previous live set survives in the data root until the replacement rename confirms. The instance lock (std File::try_lock) is acquired once and held for the process lifetime; app-store builds expose nothing (store-managed voice). A relaunch failure after a completed restore is reported truthfully as event=restored_norelaunch (exit 6), never plain restored. Restore is reachable from the desktop-only Help item "Roll Back to Mark {version}…", the renderer confirmation card (three disclosures, cancel is a no-op), and the pre-boot --rollback CLI flag (validity exit 7, live-instance probe with nonce-matched request/ack delegation or decline exit 6, TTY y/N with --yes for scripts, machine-readable MARK_ROLLBACK line, exits 0/3/4/5/6/7 with code 2 left to clap); the declined advice names both lock-holder cases (a running GUI — quit it; another headless restore — wait for it to finish) instead of R-5's quit-only line. The mid-swap writer bound for the bundle's parent directory widens R-3's same-user phrasing to same-user/admin-group (/Applications is group-admin-writable; any writer able to plant the aside has simpler attacks, such as replacing Mark.app itself). C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES adds the structured restore-outcome fact channel and the localized rollback-feedback surface: when a completed restore's preferences step fails (the logged-and-skipped site), the restore writes a minimal restore-outcome.json marker at the rollback data root itself — root-level, never inside the live/ set the restore consumes — carrying {prefs:"skipped", error (char-boundary-safe capped), at (unix seconds)}; the write is best-effort (a failed marker write changes no restore outcome), stale markers are removed at restore start at both entries, and a preferences-successful restore writes nothing. The read-and-clear mt_rollback_restore_outcome command (registered at the four boot-parity gate sites: m001_validate.rs REGISTERED_COMMANDS, main.rs generate_handler!, the renderer IPC contract types and the regenerated tauri.v2.json fixture) hands the fact to the restored session exactly once. Renderer feedback: a failed GUI restore raises the localized rollback.restoreFailedTitle/Body error notice (source rollback; the raw Rust detail stays on the console marker, never interpolated), the confirmation card awaits the store's CONFIRM_ROLLBACK (a component-level rejection is console hygiene only — the store owns user feedback), and the restored session's RUN_LAUNCH_CHECK shows the rollback.prefsSkippedTitle/Body sticky warning exactly once for a fresh (≤ 48 h) skip record — gated-off updater settings, a stale record and a broken fact channel stay console-quiet. The CLI stderr human lines stay English (recorded decision: the CLI is a developer surface; every GUI-visible string goes through the ten-locale store).

M-071.Name: StatsGateway
M-071.Summary: Redirect-only counting routes plus one keyed aggregate-readout JSON route (the documented exception) for the update funnel (C-UPDATER-STATS counting, C-STATS-READOUT readout), every counted event additionally pushed best-effort to the owner's analytics dashboard (C-STATS-DASH-PUSH): a Cloudflare Worker (tools/stats-gateway/worker.mjs, deployed owner-side on updates.mark.xronocode.com with workers_dev disabled) whose /feed route counts one check datapoint (day/os/from — the values Tauri's {{current_version}} and {{target}} placeholders substitute; os validated against the bare-OS table {darwin, windows}) and 302-redirects to the GitHub latest.json manifest, and whose /pkg/{platform}/{version} route counts one pkg datapoint (day/platform/version; platform against {darwin-aarch64, windows-x86_64}) and 302-redirects to the deterministic GitHub release asset. GET-only, exactly-the-expected-parameters, strict x.y.z validation, every Location derived (never reflected — not an open redirector), unknown input on the counting routes a plain 404 with zero datapoints, the AE write inside waitUntil (best-effort — a binding failure changes no response), and Cloudflare edge metadata never read.
